extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, applicant organizations' sponsored programs staff, and prospective NIH peer reviewers / SRG members
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing how NIH Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) perform the first-level peer review of grant applications: roles, review criteria, scoring, reviewer responsibilities, confidentiality, and post-review outcomes. Useful for applicants preparing submissions and scientists serving as reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the overall impact that the proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact scores reflect the reviewers’ overall assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. Each assigned reviewer gives a preliminary Overall Impact score before the meeting; for discussed applications each eligible panelist gives a final Overall Impact score. A final Overall Impact score is the mean of final impact scores multiplied by 10, producing a 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact) scale. Preliminary Overall Impact scores are often used to determine which applications are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Established review criteria (stated in the funding opportunity) for which reviewers assign individual criterion scores; these scored criteria contribute to the Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reviewer uses their own judgment to determine how each criterion weighs into the Overall Impact score unless specified differently in the funding opportunity. Criterion scores typically use a numerical 1–9 scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) in whole numbers (no decimals). Individual criterion scores from assigned reviewers are provided to the applicant in the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria that do not receive individual criterion scores but do contribute to the Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some additional criteria must be considered acceptable before NIH can award a grant (for example, protections for human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazards). Reviewers should comment on these issues even though they may not have separate numeric scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Items that do not receive individual criterion scores and do not contribute to the Overall Impact score, but provide programmatic input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to seek input on programmatic issues that do not directly reflect scientific/technical merit. Examples: whether an application's budget is sufficiently justified, or whether the project could be completed for a smaller budget or in fewer years than requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale for most criteria and overall impact, with 1 = exceptional and 9 = poor; final Overall Impact scores are computed as mean*10 to yield 10–90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores are whole numbers (no decimals). For discussed applications final Overall Impact scores are the mean of final impact scores from eligible members multiplied by 10. Not Discussed (ND) applications (typically bottom-half, unanimously judged less competitive) do not receive a numerical final Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned reviewer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: At least three reviewers are assigned to each application; assigned reviewers read the application thoroughly, prepare written critiques, and assign preliminary criterion and Overall Impact scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the meeting assigned reviewers write a critique summarizing strengths and weaknesses and assign a preliminary Overall Impact score. At the meeting the primary reviewer presents the application and begins discussion; the other two assigned reviewers may provide additional comments. All panelists not in conflict discuss and score the application. Tip for applicants: make it easy for reviewers who may be scanning your application to find relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections, inclusion, and specific compliance recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers make recommendations concerning protections for human subjects; inclusion of women, minorities, and children in clinical research; welfare of vertebrate animals; and other applicable compliance areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific guidance for reviewers on Human Subjects Protection, Inclusion, Human Embryonic Stem Cells, Vertebrate Animals. These areas may be treated as additional review criteria that must be acceptable for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise and Resources factor
rubrics_metrics.description: An example of a review factor that may be evaluated non-numerically (e.g., sufficient / not sufficient) for many research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some elements (like expertise and resources) may be evaluated as categorical assessments rather than numeric criterion scores depending on the grant type and funding opportunity instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications and conduct expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are scientists vetted for appropriate expertise and potential conflicts, expected to provide objective, fair, timely reviews free from inappropriate influences, and to maintain confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are recruited for authority in their field, dedication to high-quality fair and objective reviews, ability to work collegially, and balanced expertise. They must declare conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality of peer review information, and follow NIH policies. Applicants may not contact reviewers or attempt to influence reviews; there are consequences for such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the designated federal official for each SRG responsible for ensuring objective and fair initial peer review and compliance with laws, regulations, and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO assigns reviewers, gives reviewers access (except conflicted members), actively manages the meeting to ensure fair and effective review, manages conflicts of interest, prepares a resume of discussion for all applications to accurately reflect score-driving elements, and may permit federal officials with a need-to-know to attend meetings with advance approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting procedures and discussion flow
rubrics_metrics.description: How applications are handled during the SRG meeting: conflicted reviewers leave, primary reviewer presents, panel discusses, and eligible panelists score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the SRO opens the meeting conflicted reviewers are asked to leave before the group reviews an individual application. The primary reviewer presents; other assigned reviewers may add comments. All non-conflicted panelists participate in discussion and scoring. The SRO and chair facilitate and manage discussion to ensure compliance and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Discussed (ND) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications unanimously judged by the SRG to be less competitive (typically bottom half) are designated Not Discussed and do not receive a numerical final Overall Impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ND status usually indicates the application will not be discussed at the meeting and will not receive a final numeric Overall Impact score; assigned reviewers still provide their critiques and preliminary scores which are included in the summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement contents and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, applicants receive an impact score and a summary statement prepared by the SRO, which includes specified elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement typically includes Impact Score and Percentile (if applicable), a brief summary of the SRG discussion, criterion scores from assigned reviewers, bulleted critiques (strengths and weaknesses) from the assigned reviewer, budget recommendations, and any administrative comments. NIH typically releases scores in eRA Commons within 3 business days and uploads the summary statement within about 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile and ranking information
rubrics_metrics.description: For many applications the summary statement includes a percentile that ranks an application's impact score relative to others reviewed by that committee over current and the preceding two review rounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles permit comparison across scientific review committees with different scoring behaviors. A lower percentile (e.g., 5th percentile) indicates higher relative merit within that committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and applicant organizations may appeal initial review results only on specified grounds related to flaws in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are allowed if, after review of the summary statement, the applicant believes the review process was flawed due to bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by reviewers that could have substantially altered the outcome. Appeals do not apply to funding decisions, MERIT award extension decisions, or technical evaluations of R&D contract projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of other federal officials in meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal officials with a need-to-know may attend review meetings with advance approval from the SRO to provide programmatic or grants management input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These officials attend at the SRO's discretion; attendance is permitted only when necessary and with advance approval, and such staff may provide programmatic or grants management input rather than acting as reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer deliverables (critique and scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers prepare a written critique and assign numerical scores for scored review criteria as directed by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should summarize strengths and weaknesses and provide the rationale for assigned scores. The assigned reviewers' bulleted critiques and criterion scores become part of the summary statement shared with applicants.
